simple.meaning: נֶכֶס (nekeç) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a brother in the family line and in connection with kingship.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Joshua, 2 Chronicles, Ecclesiastes, beginning at Joshua 22:8. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֶכֶס (H5233) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows נֶכֶס through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: נֶכֶס (nekeç) / H5233 is tracked through Joshua 22:8, 2 Chronicles 1:11, 2 Chronicles 1:12, Ecclesiastes 5:18. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: and spoke to them, saying, “Return with much wealth to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with bronze, with iron, and with very much clothing. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers.”

timeline.evidenceText: and spoke to them, saying, “Return with much wealth to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with bronze, with iron, and with very much clothing. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers.”

God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you, nor yet have you asked for long life; but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king,
therefore wisdom and knowledge is granted to you. I will give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had who have been before you had, and none after you will have.”

Behold, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion.

a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

definitions.full: H5233. nekes [ נֶ֫כֶס ] noun masculine Josh 22:8 only plural נְכָסִים riches, treasures (probably Assyrian or Aramaic loan-word, compare Assyrian nikâsu , property , wealth , gain , Dl HWB 463 , Syriac wealth ; on derivation from Assyrian nikâsu , cut off , hew down , behead , etc., Syriac slay , נְכַס ᵑ7 , Late Hebrew נָכַס id. , through meaning cattle for slaughter , compare Frä 98 Hpt Hebraica.iii (Jan.1887), 107 ff. Schw Idioticon 120f. Brock ad voc .); — 22:8 (P), 2Chr 1:11-12 , Eccl 6:2 (all || כָּבוֺד עשֶׁר, ), 5:18 (|| עשֶׁר ).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to accumulate ;
